subject: Competitive on-ramp credit and runtime fit conversation
messages:
From: Maya Kaplan <maya.kaplan@gildatech.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sun, 17 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Competitive on-ramp / pricing parity question

Hi Rishi,

Thanks for taking a minute — quick one. We are late-stage evaluating Redwood for inference (pilot of ~120M tokens/mo, mix of chat + embeddings). A competitor (CloudWave) has offered GildaTech a 30% list discount for the first 6 months, plus an additional 3 months of onboarding credits that effectively reduce our unit cost during migration. Our procurement team asked whether Redwood can provide parity or an alternate on-ramp that makes the operational switch neutral for the rest of the year.

Two points we care about: 1) Can you match the economic on-ramp (credits/discount) for an expedited migration? 2) What is the runtime fit risk — specifically KV cache portability and estimated cutover windows for our stack (low-latency chat + 1.2k qps embedding calls)?

I attached the RFP and current usage snapshot. Happy to hop on a call if easier.

Thanks,
Maya Kaplan
Head of ML Systems | GildaTech
maya.kaplan@gildatech.com
Attachment: Gilda_RFP_Jan2026.pdf
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
To: Maya Kaplan <maya.kaplan@gildatech.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sun, 17 May 2026 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Competitive on-ramp / pricing parity question

Maya — thanks for the context and the RFP. Short answer: we can structure a competitive on-ramp that gets you cost parity or better within a slightly different construct than a straight list discount.

High-level options we typically offer for situations like this:
- Time-bound onboarding credits (applied against usage for first 60–90 days)
- Step-down volume credits tied to committed throughput for months 3–12
- Dedicated migration sprint (engineer-days) to reduce cutover risk and shorten the effective migration window

I’m looping in Lauren (runtime/product) and Aditya (pricing) — Lauren, can you confirm KV portability and any gotchas for their workload? Aditya, I’ll need a quick model to show 60/90-day credit vs. a 30% competitor discount so we can have a counteroffer ready tomorrow. I attached a starter model.

Next steps: we can propose a counter that blends a 25% credit for first 90 days + a 2-week dedicated migration sprint (reduced engineering hours billed as credits) and a 60-day exit option if we materially miss latency targets. Would that be helpful?

- Rishi
Attachment: price_parity_model.xlsx
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Maya Kaplan <maya.kaplan@gildatech.com>
Date: Mon, 18 May 2026 10:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Competitive on-ramp / pricing parity question

On Sun, May 17, 2026 at 11:02 AM Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com> wrote:
> I’m looping in Lauren (runtime/product) and Aditya (pricing) — Lauren, can you confirm KV portability and any gotchas for their workload?

Maya / team — quick technical note from runtime:
- KV cache: if GildaTech is using a compatible transformer family and not relying on custom tokenizer state, prefix/KV export is feasible. We will need to run a short validation pass on a 24–48 hour slice to confirm cache hit expectations.
- Latency: with Dedicated capacity and matched instance types, we expect sub-30ms median for chat and embedding p95s under 1s for their volumes once batching is tuned.
- Cutover: realistic blue/green cutover with traffic split can be done in 48–72 hours if we run a preflight integration week (logs, tracing, metrics hooks).

Operational risk mitigations I recommend: 1) migration sprint (2 weeks engineering + runbook), 2) two-week parallel run with guarded routing, 3) an SLA clause for first 90 days with defined rollback triggers.

I’ve attached a one-pager runtime-fit summary and a draft SOW for onboarding that outlines effort and deliverables.

Lauren Bishop
Senior Product Manager, Runtime
Redwood Inference
Attachment: runtime-fit-summary.pdf; onboarding-sow-draft.docx
From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwoodinference.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Maya Kaplan <maya.kaplan@gildatech.com>
Date: Mon, 18 May 2026 15:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Competitive on-ramp / pricing parity question

Rishi / Lauren — ran numbers against their usage profile. Two quick scenarios in the model:
1) 30% competitor discount for 180 days — net onboarding benefit = $72k (est), lower renewal anchor
2) Redwood counter: 25% credit for first 90 days + 2-week migration sprint credit (engineer-day equivalent) + a step-down 10% rebate months 4–12 — net onboarding benefit ~ $78k with higher lifetime revenue due to anchoring on committed throughput.

Pros of our counter: faster migration (fewer ops hours), better control on long-term TCO because credits step down faster, and we can attach a success SLO to maintain economics.

Cons: perception — 25% vs 30% headline may feel weaker, so we should present the total value (credits + migration sprint + faster time-to-value) and include a short pilot SLA.

I’ve updated price_parity_model.xlsx with the two scenarios and sensitivity to token growth. Recommend proposing the hybrid counter: 25% credit for 90 days, 2-week migration sprint credited, 60-day opt-out.

- Aditya
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 19 May 2026 17:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Competitive on-ramp / pricing parity question

Thanks for the analysis — I reviewed the model and the runtime notes. Approved to proceed with a customer-facing counter. Final terms to offer GildaTech: 
- 25% usage credit applied to invoice for first 90 days
- 2-week dedicated migration sprint (up to 10 engineer-days) credited to onboarding costs
- 60-day opt-out clause if we miss agreed p95 latency targets for two consecutive weeks
- Renewal pricing anchored to post-credit effective rates with a step-down rebate months 4–12 as outlined by Aditya

Please prepare the term sheet and the short one-pager that frames the total value (credit + migration sprint + SLA). Share the HubSpot deal link when ready and put the approved-term-sheet.pdf in the drive. I approved the concession because the migration sprint materially reduces churn risk and preserves long-term ARPU.

Marissa Cole
VP Sales, Redwood Inference
Attachment: approved-term-sheet.pdf
